newsitem.title: USA: Port of N.Y./N.J. to cut fees on local cargo.
newsitem.headline: Port of N.Y./N.J. to cut fees on local cargo.

text.p: The Port of New York and New Jersey will cut local cargo charges by 17 percent as of February 1, 1997, port officials said on Thursday.

Charges for cargo originating from within or destined for points within 260 miles of the port will be lowered to $2.90 per ton, from their current level of $3.50 per ton, the International Longshoremen's Association and the New York Shipping Association (NYSA) said in a joint statement.

"This assessment reduction is one more step in our continuing effort to make sure the Port of New York and New Jersey is a competitive, productive place for the world's shipping community to do business," the statement said.
The recent retirement of 518 of the port's 3,000 unionized dockworkers, whose benefits are funded by the cargo charges, made the fee reduction possible, it said.
In 1995, charges on inland cargo -- goods originating at, or bound for North American markets outside the 260 mile perimeter -- were lowered to $1 a ton, from $1.85.
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey applauded the announcement, calling it "excellent news" for the port and the region's economy.

"Last year's labor agreement and today's fee reduction ensures shippers improved service for less cost," Port Authority executive director George Marlin said in a statement. "It should be especially important in attracting waterborne shipments from Asia to the Port of New York and New Jersey."
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
